transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Aurora VP Eng), Sana Patel (Aurora SRE Lead), Tom Rivera (Aurora CTO)

Summary:
Quick follow-up postmortem review after last week's incident where Aurora saw ~30 minutes of elevated 5xxs and tail latency spikes on the Redwood hosted route. Focus on RCA, short-term mitigations (routing/fallbacks), and medium-term reliability improvements for their private/dedicated migration.

Topics:
- Root cause (KV cache invalidation + routing fallback config)
- Impact and customer metrics (errors, user-facing impact)
- Immediate mitigations and rollback plan
- Dedicated vs hosted routing choices and failover behavior
- Security/audit requests and evidence sharing
- Next steps and owners

Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight 30-45 minutes. The goal is to run through the postmortem and next steps. Priya and I will walk through what we learned.
[01:12] Priya: Hi all. Quick note: transcription might have some names wrong, sorry in advance. So to start, root cause was a KV cache invalidation that triggered when a rolling kernel upgrade touched a subset of nodes and the fallback routing pushed traffic to the hosted route with a mismatched model variant.
[02:05] Marcus: Can you unpack "KV cache invalidation" in simple terms? Our SREs saw a bunch of misses then errors.
[02:38] Priya: Yeah. The runtime keeps per-request KV caches for prompt prefixes to speed up decoding. During a maintenance window a subset of gateway hosts evicted their prefix caches because of a concurrent config push; those hosts then experienced much higher compute per request which ran into a soft quota and started returning 5xx throttles.
[03:10] Sana: Right, the symptom we saw was a jump in p99 latency and 5xxs at 22:14 UTC. It correlated with a config rollout from your side, though we also had a spike in traffic at the same time.
[03:35] Alex: Exactly. Two compounding factors: the cache invalidation and a slightly aggressive routing policy that fell back to the hosted pool which had a different quantization/profile and higher tail latency. We should've bound the fallback to compatible variants.
[04:50] Tom: Just to be clear, were user prompts lost or just delayed/errors? We had some support tickets saying failures on request.
[05:12] Priya: Mostly transient errors — a subset of requests returned 5xx. For many clients the SDK retried and succeeded, but for time-sensitive flows you did see failures. No data exfiltration — this was compute/serving level.
[06:00] Marcus: Ok that's helpful. From our side the biggest concern is unpredictability during upgrades; can Redwood provide ways to prevent this and also better visibility when it happens?
[06:22] Alex: Absolutely. Short term: we recommend two mitigations — conservative fallback (only route to compatible model variant) and sticky routing during config rollouts; medium term: KV cache persistence across rolling upgrades and stronger preflight checks.
[07:05] Priya: Also, we'll push a change that prevents fallback to a hosted model with different quant profile unless explicitly allowed by the tenant config. That will be a small server-side guard.
[08:20] Sana: Will that be a flag we can see in the console or API? We want auditability.
[08:40] Alex: Yes, we'll add it to the rollout config and surface it in the route-level settings — and emit an event to audit logs when fallback occurs.
[09:15] Tom: Speaking of audit logs, we need the SOC2 artifact set and the request-level logs for the incident window. Who to send to?
[09:38] Alex: I'll send the SOC2 evidence bundle link and a signed log export for 22:00-23:00 UTC. Expect that by EOD Monday.
[10:10] Marcus: On the dedicated plan — if we moved to a dedicated pool would this class of problem be avoided? Our assumption is yes but want to hear nuance.
[10:55] Priya: Dedicated helps a lot, yes — isolated GPU pools mean you control the upgrade window and we won't route to hosted pools. But dedicated still uses the same runtime; if you run upgrades concurrently across your pool there are still cache eviction risks. We'll recommend schedule windows and a KV cache persistence change for dedicated customers.
[12:03] Sana: Any quick wins we can enable now to reduce blast radius?
[12:18] Alex: Two quick wins — enable per-tenant conservative fallback (we'll flip it for you) and increase prefix cache size/time-to-live for your tenant. Also enable stricter circuit-breaker thresholds so we fail fast instead of cascading.
[13:05] Marcus: How invasive is increasing TTL for cache? Any correctness concerns?
[13:25] Priya: TTL increase is safe; the main tradeoff is memory. For Aurora's traffic profile we can increase slightly without risk. We'll propose exact numbers after running a replay.
[14:10] Sana: Replay — we'll need instructions. If you provide harness, sample dataset, and expected metrics we can run it in our staging.
[14:34] Priya: We'll provide a replay harness and sample dataset. It will simulate your prefix distribution and peak QPS. We'll also provide recommended cache settings.
[15:00] Tom: On the topic of monitoring — any improvements planned to surface cache invalidations or config rollouts in real time?
[15:20] Alex: Yes, we're adding telemetry for cache miss ratios and a rollout correlation widget in the console. Not immediate but prioritized high. We'll give an ETA in the postmortem doc.
[16:45] Marcus: Request: include a timeline with exact host ids/ips affected. We need to cross-check with our ingress logs.
[17:05] Alex: We'll include host tags and a redacted host list in the log export.
[18:00] Sana: Can you confirm there was no data retention violation? We need to verify PII controls.
[18:20] Priya: Confirmed — this was serving-level; no storage or logs were exposed beyond normal request logs. We'll include the audit trail showing access patterns.
[19:10] Tom: Ok, about the root cause, will you change the config rollout ordering to avoid simultaneous eviction across nodes?
[19:35] Priya: Yes, we will change rollout to stagger cache-affecting config updates and add a preflight check that simulates cache pressure.
[20:25] Marcus: Great. For the dedicated migration timeline, what's realistic?
[20:52] Alex: If you decide to move to dedicated, typical ramp is 4-6 weeks for setup and validation, less if we reuse existing model config. We'll scope a pilot first — small reserved pool + canary traffic.
[21:40] Sana: Pilot would be ideal. Also want to define SLOs upfront for error rate and p95 latency.
[22:05] Priya: We'll propose SLO targets and a monitoring dashboard for the pilot.
[23:10] Marcus: Any permanent code changes on our side? We don't want big SDK changes.
[23:35] Alex: No SDK changes required for the fixes we propose. The only thing we might ask is to enable a conservative fallback flag and accept the slightly different latency profile in return for stability.
[24:10] Tom: Are there any security concerns with the audit logs export? We need signed artifacts.
[24:40] Alex: Exports will be signed and delivered over your S3 presigned link. We'll also provide a checksum and reference in the SOC2 bundle.
[25:30] Sana: Regarding the incident timeline in your postmortem, we need: trigger, detection, mitigation, root cause, corrective actions, and timeline with host ids.
[25:55] Priya: We'll include all those sections. We already have an internal draft and will finalize it for distribution.
[26:30] Marcus: For the short term, please flip the conservative fallback and increase TTL; we can run replay and then decide on dedicated.
[26:55] Alex: Agreed. Action items we'll follow up on in the notes.
[27:40] Priya: Quick technical note: the fallback guard will check model architecture, quantization profile, and kernel compatibility. If mismatch, it will refuse fallback and instead queue requests or failover within same compatibility class.
[29:00] Tom: That sounds good. Any risk that refusing fallback increases errors?
[29:20] Priya: Potentially, but the intention is to fail fast so clients can retry or use their own fallback; we can tune circuit-breakers to prevent user-visible failures.
[30:05] Marcus: Can we get a short runbook for our on-call to follow during similar incidents? Steps, who to ping, and quick mitigations?
[30:30] Alex: Yes, we'll include a runbook and a truncated checklist: flip conservative fallback, bump cache TTL, check host health, engage Redwood SE.
[31:10] Sana: On legal/procurement — we may want contractual language for maintenance windows and rollback SLAs. We'll have our procurement team follow up.
[31:35] Alex: Noted; we'll block a follow-up with legal if needed.
[32:10] Marcus: Any blockers on Redwood's side to push the conservative fallback and the logging changes?
[32:30] Priya: No blockers — small server-side config changes and audit-event emission. We can roll the fallback guard in a patch release next week; logging changes might take two weeks.
[33:20] Tom: Awesome. Can we have a short executive summary for our leadership?
[33:40] Alex: We'll include an exec summary at the top of the postmortem doc.
[34:10] Priya: Also note: we'll include proposed SLOs for pilot and recommended cache params.
[35:00] Marcus: Ok, I'm comfortable with the plan if we get the postmortem and the replay harness. We'll aim to run replay by Friday.
[35:20] Alex: Great. Any final questions?
[36:00] Sana: One last ask — can we have a short table of the host-side metrics to look for during replay?
[36:25] Priya: Yes — we'll include p95/p99 latency, cache miss ratio, CPU/GPU utilization and queue depth.
[37:10] Tom: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[37:30] Alex: Thanks; we'll recap next steps.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Alex to share root-cause writeup and timeline by 2027-05-17 (includes host ids, event timeline, and planned mitigations)
- Priya to share replay harness, sample dataset, recommended cache TTL and circuit-breaker settings by 2027-05-16
- Alex to deliver SOC2 evidence bundle + signed log export for incident window by 2027-05-17 EOD
- Aurora (Sana) to run replay and return metrics by 2027-05-21
- Schedule joint dedicated vs hosted benchmark (week of 2027-05-24) — Alex/Priya to propose times

Closing: Meeting ended 15:46 UTC.

Notes about transcription: there are a few misheard proper nouns; names of internal hosts will be provided in the signed export rather than in this transcript to protect redaction.
